chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, all together from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Sukayn al-Nakha'i

— and he used to engage in devotional worship and had abandoned women (marriage), perfume, and (good) food. So he wrote to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) asking him about that, and he (the Imam) wrote back to him:

'As for your words regarding women, you have indeed known what the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) had of women; and as for your words regarding food, the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) used to eat meat and honey.'

key_terms.الطِّيب: perfume, fragrance — one of the Prophet's beloved sunnah items
key_terms.النِّسَاء: women, specifically here referring to marriage

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about a man who abandoned women, perfume, and good food in devotion?
ai.summary: This hadith records the response of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) to a man named Sukayn al-Nakha'i, who had adopted an extreme ascetic lifestyle by abandoning marriage, perfume, and wholesome food. The Imam's letter corrected this misguided piety by invoking the prophetic example: the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) himself had multiple wives and regularly ate meat and honey. This teaching reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that excessive renunciation of lawful pleasures (zuhd from the halal) goes against the prophetic sunnah, and that moderation and engagement with the world are Islamically preferred over monastic withdrawal.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzaan, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameedm,

(It has been narrated) from Sukeyn Al-Nakhaie and he used to worship and neglect the women, and the perfume, and the (good) food. So he wrote to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> asking him<sup>asws</sup> about that, so he<sup>asws</sup> wrote to him:

‘As for your words regarding the women, so you have known what was for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> from the women, and as for your words regarding the (good) food, so Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to eat the meat and the honey’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ibrahim ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid who has narrated the following:
“Sukayn al-Nakha‘iy worshipped and had given up women, perfume and food. He wrote to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and asked him (the Imam) about it. He (the Imam) wrote to him in answer,

‘About your words concerning women, take notice about the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, how many women he (the Messenger of Allah) had, and about food you must take notice that the Messenger of Allah ate meat with honey.’”
